title: Adaptive invite throttling with per-team emergency admin revocation and audit sink
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We observe bursts of automated/org-wide invite attempts and occasional misconfigured admin invites that bypass intended SSO/domain controls. Current invite quota logic is flat and global which makes it hard to mitigate blast radius and to quickly remove a runaway admin. Goal: Implement an adaptive invite throttler that dynamically adjusts per-org and per-team invite throughput based on recent traffic and risk signals, and provide a fast, auditable emergency admin revoke flow that disables invite privileges at the team level while preserving auditability. Also add a dedicated audit sink for invite- and admin-related events to the security SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) with an immutable schema for downstream compliance and incident response.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Throttle enforces per-org and per-team invite limits with exponential backoff and decays over 1h; 2) Risk score inputs (SSO status, domain verification, invite velocity, IP reputation) used to lower thresholds for high-risk orgs; 3) One-click emergency revoke for team admins that immediately toggles an RBAC v2 override blocking invite-affecting actions and logs a high-priority audit event; 4) Audit sink receives structured events (invite.request, invite.approval, invite.throttle, admin.revoke, admin.restore) with required fields and retention policy applied; 5) End-to-end tests and canary rollout on a subset of orgs with no >1% false-positive customer impact during canary.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy throttler as sidecar rule on routing plane for 5% of orgs (low-risk and internal). Phase 2: Enable risk signals and emergency revoke UI in Console behind feature flag. Phase 3: Full rollout with SIEM export and alerting thresholds. Provide a rollback toggle and throttler disabled mode preserved for emergency ops.
implementation_notes: - Throttler algorithm: token-bucket per-org and per-team with adaptive refill rate = base_rate * risk_multiplier. Risk multiplier derived from simple weighted sum of signals (SSO_enabled: 0.6, domain_verified: 0.7, invite_velocity zscore: 0.5, ip_reputation_score: 0.8). - Emergency revoke: RBAC v2 override flag stored in authz store (fast-path cache invalidated via pub/sub). Revoke action creates immutable audit event and issues short-lived token revocation for current sessions. - Audit schema: event_type, timestamp, org_id, team_id, actor_id, actor_type, ip, user_agent, invite_count_window, risk_score, action_id, outcome, trace_id. Serialize to JSONL, push to security-kinesis -> Splunk forwarding lambda. - Backwards compatibility: non-SSO orgs default to stricter invite limits; SSO-enforced orgs get relaxed thresholds only after domain verification and SAML metadata validation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives throttle legitimate onboarding spikes. Mitigation: gradual decay window, manual override for support to temporarily bump limits, and canary with detailed telemetry. Risk: Revoke could lock out required admins during incident. Mitigation: revoke is scoped to invite capabilities not full admin rights, and includes emergency restore workflow with audit and audit-approval gating. Risk: Audit pipeline adds latency. Mitigation: async fire-and-forget with retry queue and backpressure metrics.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket logic and risk multiplier computation. Integration tests simulating spike patterns and SSO vs non-SSO behaviour. E2E canary with synthetic orgs and shadow mode for 48h to compare decisions vs current system. Chaos test: simulate pub/sub delay to validate revoke eventual-consistency and ensure support override works.
rollout_and_monitoring: Canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% over 3 weeks. Monitor: invite_throttle_rate, admin_revoke_count, support_override_rate, false_positive_rate (customer complaints/day), SIEM alert rates. Dashboards: Console -> Security -> Invite Control (link to dashboard). Pager thresholds for edge cases set with runbook.
